claims.classification: Sharp energy-only single-band activation timescale for smooth local full unforced periodic Navier-Stokes families; not regularity or novelty.
proved_in_stated_scope: On fixed T3 with nu>0 and E0>0, for a fixed smooth annular multiplier Q_N=chi(D/N), every smooth fullNS solution obeys a_N(t)-a_N(s)<=C E0 N^(5/2)(t-s). Any specified positive amplitude rise therefore costs at least its increment divided by C E0 N^(5/2).

For each fixed E0 and nu there is a fixed eta in(0,E0) and a family of real meanzero smooth full unforced periodic NS solutions with initial Fourier support[N,2N] and exactly zero target band(2.05N,2.2N), whose first eta-band-energy hitting time satisfies c N^(-5/2)<=T_N<=C N^(-5/2) for all sufficiently large dyadic N.

The family has exact initial energyE0, genuine full nonlinear evolution on the whole stated window, and viscous energy loss<=C'nu N^(-1/2)->0. The small-delta packet calculation, periodization/product limit and uniform Duhamel O(tau^2) remainder are all included.

Thus a universal positive lower bound c*(nu N^2)^(-1) for this activation time, depending only on the stated fixed energy/viscosity/filter/threshold and not on initial high norms, is false. More generally a uniform energy-only power exponent alpha<5/2 cannot replace5/2 for this positive threshold.
limitations: Only first activation into an initially empty output band is tested, not residence after arrival.
Initial energy is already at frequency comparable to N. This is one high-high-to-comparable-high spectral-gap filling, not a low-frequency-origin or repeated cascade.
Initial data and their high Sobolev/critical norms vary withN. No one fixed initial datum, mature-history bound, infinite cascade, singularity or global regularity counterexample is constructed.
